enrichments.obs_text: The codes of God's thoughts are H4284 (thought, device; plan, purpose) and H7454 (purpose, aim, thought). The lexicon bears out thoughts as purposes, here the Lord's own, set against man's in Isa 55:8 and Isa 55:9 and unknown to the nations in Mic 4:12.

The code of conceiving evil is H2029 (to conceive, become pregnant, bear). The lexicon gives only the bodily sense; Job 15:35, Isa 33:11 and Isa 59:4 turn it to trouble and mischief formed within and brought out: the figure is the verses', not the lexicon's.

The codes of conceiving a child are H2029 (to conceive), H2030A (pregnant), H2232 (to sow; to be made pregnant), H3179 (to be hot, conceive), G4815 (to become pregnant, conceive), G2602 (foundation, with the seed in Heb 11:11) and G4690G (seed, offspring); G1722 (in) and G2192 (to have) make the Greek phrase of having in the womb. The lexicon bears out a bodily conceiving with no act of thought.

The code behind opinion in Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 is G0991 (to see, look at). The lexicon gives seeing; the phrase is not looking at a person's standing, so no view is held: the English opinion is not the code's sense.

The codes of a declared opinion are H1843 (knowledge, opinion; judgment) in Job 32:6, Job 32:10 and Job 32:17 and H3820A (inner man, mind, heart) in Pro 18:2, where the fool's opinion is what is in his heart. The lexicon bears out a view held and spoken.
The code of thought in Jon 1:6 is H0194 (perhaps, peradventure). The lexicon gives a particle of possibility; it carries no thinking, and the giving of thought is the captain's hope about the god.
The code of with no thought of war in Mic 2:8 is H7725G (to return, turn back). The lexicon gives returning; the English thought is not in the code.
The code of well thought of in 1Ti 3:7 is G3141 (testimony; good reputation). The lexicon bears out a good report from others, not a thought of the overseer.

The codes of thinking as the mind's mode are G1261 (reasoning, thought) in Rom 1:21, G5424 (thinking, understanding) in 1Cor 14:20 and G1771 (attitude, thought, intention) in 1Pe 4:1. G2532 (and) is a connective in the unit. The lexicon bears out the mind's way of working, with futility or maturity named by the verses.

The code of what do you think is G1380 (to think, consider, regard; an action of the mind and heart for processing information into understanding and choices). The lexicon bears out asking for a judgment the hearer forms, in Mat 17:25, Mat 18:12, Mat 21:28, Mat 22:17, Mat 22:42, Luk 10:36 and Joh 11:56.
enrichments.grounds: an action of the mind and heart

enrichments.obs_text: The code of what seems best is H5869I (eye; as showing mental qualities), with H0413 (to, toward). The lexicon bears out the eye as the seat of judgment in the idiom good in your eyes, in Num 36:6, 2Sa 10:3, 1Ch 19:3, Jer 40:4, Jer 40:5 and 2Sa 3:19.

The codes of a thought quoted as inner speech are H0559 (to say; to say in one's heart, to think, to intend), G1260 (to reason, deliberate) and G3004G (to say). H0834A (which), H0853 (the object marker) and H3588A (that, for) are small words in the units. The lexicon bears out saying in one's heart as the form of the thought, as in 1Sa 16:6, 1Sa 18:11, 1Sa 18:17 and 1Sa 20:3.
enrichments.grounds: to say in one's heart, to think

enrichments.obs_text: The codes of planning or intending are H2803I (to plan, devise, mean), H2803J (to think, plan), H1819 (to imagine, think) and H5452 (to think, intend). The lexicon bears out devising and purpose, in Isa 10:7, Jer 23:27, Dan 7:25, Num 33:56, 1Sa 18:25 and Job 6:26.

The codes of giving thought are H2803I and H2803J (to think, account), H2142 (to remember, call to mind), H0995 (to discern, consider), H1819 (to imagine, think), H6245B (to think), G3049 (to count, consider), G3421 (to remember, fix the thoughts upon), G3539 (to understand, reflect), G1760 (to reflect on) and G1761 (reflection). H1931 (he) is a pronoun in a unit. The lexicon bears out attention of the mind turned to a matter or person, as in Phili 4:8, Heb 11:15, Lam 1:9 and Mat 9:4.
enrichments.grounds: to remember, recall, call to mind

enrichments.obs_text: The codes of reckoning something as so are G3049 (to credit, count, reckon), G2233 (to think, consider, count), G2919 (to decide, consider) and H2803J (to think, account). G1161 (but) is a connective in a unit. The lexicon bears out a judgment that counts a thing as of a kind, in Rom 14:14, Gen 38:15, Act 26:8 and the others.
The code of being minded is G5426 (to think, regard, hold an opinion; to set one's mind on; to have a certain attitude). The lexicon bears out a set of mind, in Rom 12:3, Phili 3:15 and 1Cor 13:11.

The codes of thoughts as purposes are H4284 (thought, device; plan, purpose), H4209 (purpose, device, plot) and H1902H (meditation, plotting). The lexicon bears out purpose and device, placed by the verses in the heart, as in Gen 6:5 and 1Ch 28:9.

The codes of thoughts that arise and are held are G1261 (reasoning, thought), G1270 (thought), G1271 (mind, thinking), G1761 (reflection), G3540 (mind, thought; scheme, design), H4093 (knowledge, thought; place of knowledge), H5587B (disquietings), H6248 (thought, idea), H7454 (purpose, thought), H7476 (thought), H7808 (thought), H8312 (disquieting thoughts) and H2808 (reasoning). H1697G and H1697I (word, thing), H1961 (to be) and G3588 (the) stand in the units. The lexicon bears out thoughts as what the mind holds, some of them disquieting, as in 1Cor 2:11, 2Cor 10:5, Amo 4:13 and Dan 2:29.

The codes of supposing something to be so are G1380 (to think, imagine, suppose, presume), G3543 (to suppose, presume, expect), G3633 (to think, suppose, presume), H0559 (to say in one's heart, to think), H1819 (to imagine, think) and H7200H (to see, consider). The lexicon bears out a belief held, which the verses test, as in 1Cor 3:18, 1Cor 10:12 and 1Cor 14:37.
